summary: A 1923 frame cab and 1940 L-4 cab on a pole tower in Lincoln County, Montana; now in ruins, and a trail listing says the site is closed.

facts.design: 10x10 ft frame cab with roof platform (1923); 10 ft pole tower with L-4 cab (1940); separate L-6 cab about 1 mile northeast
facts.status_note: The register says the tower now lies in ruins after vandalism and decay; the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Montana list still shows it standing.

access.note: A travel listing for the Elk Patrol Trail says the old structure is now closed to the public; a Visit Montana listing for the Elk Mountain Trail does not mention a closure.

notes_for_editor: Location: the record's NHLR point and the FFLA 'Elk Patrol' point (48.46258, -114.89668) are about 1.56 km apart, and no source here explains why. The FFLA Montana list also has a separate 'Elk Mountain' entry (Lincoln, 48.45553, -114.91496, marked 'Tower Gone') at the NHLR point's coordinates, so it may duplicate this record or us-mt-elk-mountain; a human should check. Kind: the record says 'ground', but the 1940 structure is a 10 ft pole tower with an L-4 cab; the 1923 cab is described only as a frame cab with roof platform. Access: the two trail listings differ; one says closed, the other is silent on closure. No staffing or fire history found, so none is claimed. Photos: the NHLR photos are already on the record; firelookout.com credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum, Gary Weber and Luke Channer, but no image URL was found, so none added.
